claims.text: Progress does not go in a straight line, so focus on one thing only is good advice that assumes something false: that the shortest path to a goal runs through that goal.
claims.quote: "Focus on one thing only" is good advice that assumes the shortest path to a goal runs through that goal. It often does not.

claims.text: The owner does focus, with undivided attention, on whichever thing has the highest leverage, chosen because it has users and feedback loops now.
claims.quote: Undivided attention, on one thing at a time, chosen because it has users and feedback loops now.

claims.text: The owner's measure is always whether he is getting better, discovering new capabilities at the right altitude; the commit log says the newsroom, he says RiskMandate, and the commit log is the more interesting half.
claims.quote: Someone looking at the commit log would say I am focused on the newsroom. I would say I am focused on RiskMandate

claims.text: RiskMandate is where most of the commercial opportunity is and where engagement is starting; it has technical problems to solve to work at scale, and the obvious advice is to focus on it alone.
claims.quote: RiskMandate is where most of the commercial opportunity is.

claims.text: Where the master vault's key lives, so a user can open their vault on any device without us holding it, had been a problem for about six months, with proofs of concept abandoned for failing the simplicity test.
claims.quote: has been a problem for about six months

value.unit: months the master vault key problem resisted

claims.text: Each earlier attempt was getting too complicated, and complicated is how security designs fail.
claims.quote: Each one was getting too complicated, and complicated is how security designs fail.

claims.text: It was solved in two days: a passkey's PRF output computes a door, the door holds the master vault's key, there is a door per path, and no server of ours is in the chain; built for the newsroom, it applies everywhere.
claims.quote: A passkey's PRF output computes a door; the door holds the master vault's key; there is a door per path

claims.text: The rule is to follow the users, even when the user is the owner, and the feedback loops: do the thing that gets a reaction straight away.
claims.quote: The rule I follow is to always follow the users, even when the user is me, and to follow the feedback loops

claims.text: RiskMandate's traction is real but close to forward-deployed engineering, so handing users their vault keys works at today's volumes; there is not enough momentum to solve per-user vaults, and the owner's instinct then is not to solve it.
claims.quote: There is not enough momentum to solve that problem, and my instinct when there is not enough momentum is: do not solve it.

claims.text: A problem solved before anybody needs it is solved in the abstract, and abstract solutions are where the complexity creeps in.
claims.quote: A problem solved before anybody needs it is solved in the abstract, and abstract solutions are where the complexity creeps in.

claims.text: The newsroom is the opposite: readers on every device, a reading meter, personas, an encrypted share and pay-after-you-read that only work if every reader has a vault that follows them; that momentum makes a hard problem solvable in two days.
claims.quote: momentum is what makes a hard problem solvable in two days, because every attempt gets tested by somebody who wants it to work

claims.text: The newsroom has forced the agentic workflow to mature, agents that follow up people and threads, draft, publish and keep a record; a very effective newsroom is underneath a very effective CRM and publishing workflow, which RiskMandate needs.
claims.quote: A very effective newsroom is, underneath, a very effective CRM and a very effective publishing workflow, which is exactly what RiskMandate needs.

claims.text: RiskMandate sells Agent Behaviour Policies and licences to operate, and the hardest part of selling them is showing them in action, because customer examples cannot be shared; the newsroom's agents, their policy, status reports, leak scans and release logs are the best public example.
claims.quote: is the best public example we have of a behaviour policy running in practice

claims.text: The Cyber Boardroom came first, a GenAI platform for boards with an advisor called Athena, where the owner discovered the value of personas and shaping output to the reader; what it lacked was somewhere to store confidential data, which is what sgit became.
claims.quote: Ironically, what The Cyber Boardroom needed is what I eventually built as sgit.

claims.text: MyFeeds built personalised feeds on semantic graphs of the news, from the article to the reader's persona, and found the industry silent; it needed micropayments the industry was not ready for, and it was paused.
claims.quote: Then I took it to the industry and there was silence.

claims.text: The 2025 pieces on monetising trust and knowledge, fact provenance and micro and nano payments are the foundations the newsroom stands on; the story vault and pay after you read are those pieces, built.
claims.quote: are the foundations the newsroom now stands on

claims.text: The company created in Portugal for MyFeeds is being closed, because running a company with little revenue in Portugal is expensive in a way it is not in England, and Lithuania is being looked at for the next one.
claims.quote: running a company with little revenue in Portugal is expensive in a way it is not in England

claims.text: The owner is about to do a larger round of outreach to publishers with an end-to-end example that now exists: content, semantic graphs, a reading meter, personas, micropayments, a vault per reader, all running and open source.
claims.quote: I am about to do another, larger round of outreach to publishers and to people in the news industry.

claims.text: If the outreach does not land in 2026 the owner will try again in 2027; he does not need it to work in the news industry for the work to have been worth it, because the newsroom is already making RiskMandate better.
claims.quote: If it works, good. If it does not, I will try again in 2027.

claims.text: The newsroom has already benefited from five or ten articles written a year ago, when there was no way to build what they described; the thinking survives because it is written down and open.
claims.quote: The newsroom has already benefited from five or ten articles I wrote a year ago

value.unit: to ten articles from a year ago the newsroom stands on

claims.text: Focus, for the owner, is undivided attention on the place of highest leverage; it is not the same thing as working on only one product, and the difference is the whole of the article.
claims.quote: Focus, for me, is undivided attention on the place of highest leverage.

claims.text: The six months and the two days are the owner's account; the design, the lab and the evening it went live are in linked articles, and the earlier attempts are not published.
claims.quote: The six months and the two days are my account.

claims.text: RiskMandate's traction is described, not measured here: engagements, volumes and the move to self-service are the owner's reading of where it is.
claims.quote: RiskMandate's traction is described, not measured here.

claims.text: The Cyber Boardroom and MyFeeds are summarised from memory; the links are to what is public and the proofs of concept are not all published.
claims.quote: The Cyber Boardroom and MyFeeds are summarised from memory.

claims.text: The company move is a consideration, not a decision: Lithuania is being looked at and nothing has been registered.
claims.quote: Lithuania is being looked at; nothing has been registered.

claims.text: This is one person's method; it works because the owner writes things down and works in the open, and may not transfer to a team that does neither.
claims.quote: it may not transfer to a team that does neither

claims.text: The article came from a voice memo on 12 October 2026 at the end of a day spent mostly on voice memos, written by this site's agent in the voice of this site.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 12 October 2026, at the end of a day spent mostly on voice memos
